Adding c/n corrections changes the finite counting expression from one Gamma factor to a product and loses the earlier Riemann-count comparison; deleting prime-indexed levels changes the logarithmic asymptotic but does not improve zero locations. In both cases the exact count is still assembled from smoothly varying arctangent contributions, so level-list engineering can alter smooth density without readily producing the irregular interpolation associated with the zeros. This is evidence against the explored family, not an impossibility theorem, and supports only an unspecified need for further generalization.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Unifies two superficially different failures by locating the invariant mechanism—the smooth basis of phase contributions—and distinguishes changing aggregate density from generating oscillatory fine structure.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because it preserves both concrete routes, their different asymptotic effects, and their common obstruction while applying the critic's restriction against naming the later coupling construction.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span reports the c/n modification, its two-Gamma expression and loss of the prior comparison, similar behavior for higher inverse-power corrections, the log(N/log N) effect of prime deletion, the lack of improved zero locations, and the smooth-arctangent explanation for the negative results.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The negative results are source-reported experiments with a source-given mechanism, not a proof that all level modifications fail; the later form of the proposed generalization is not imported.

parents.title: Statewise solvability does not automatically extend to many-body integrability

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The established I-to-RD solution route does not automatically yield a many-body integrability result: the source says that several rapidity variables make extension of the map non-obvious. It separately limits renormalizability and exact solvability to the quantum-mechanical I± models. Recasting the RD coupling as boundary data in a transfer matrix makes the open problem concrete: level-dependent couplings g_(D,n) suggest that a corresponding transfer matrix, if it exists, would need more than one boundary operator. That suggestion gains a candidate representation for the obstruction but supplies no many-body map, transfer matrix, or integrability proof.
